slots.title: U.S. session recap — Sept. 21, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led the U.S. cash close on 2026-09-21, up 2.3% to 27,122.09, while the S&P 500 rose 1.5% to 7,764.22 and the Dow added 0.7% to 52,048.83.
The Russell 2000 finished up 0.5% at 2,875.36.
Headlines in the injected feed emphasized summit diplomacy and sector rotation into growth-heavy areas rather than a single macro shock.

Meta Platforms was the standout megacap percentage move:
- $META +11.3% to 741.25
- $WBD +10.8% to 30.80

) also printed a double-digit gain among active names.

Semiconductors and foundry exposure moved together in the mega-cap set.:
- $AMD +9.9% to 615.52
- $NVDA +2.3% to 227.38
- $TSM +2.4% to 445.14
- $INTC +12.1% to 121.78

rounded out the chip tape for the session.
Nasdaq Technology averaged +1.3%.

Other large tech and platform names participated without matching Meta’s magnitude:
- $MSFT +1.6% to 501.61
- $GOOGL +1.6% to 354.97

and $NVDA volume remained heavy at 109.3M shares in the quote block.
Real Estate (+1.7%) and Utilities (+1.4%) also showed positive sector averages on Nasdaq, while Basic Materials (−0.8%) and Industrials (−0.6%) lagged.

Energy equities diverged from one crude proxy.
$CVX −2.7% to 203.78 sat among mega-cap decliners as the United States Oil Fund ($USO) closed −3.7% at 148.16.
Brent crude in the cross-asset set was up 1.1% to 101.48 in the same bundle, illustrating mixed oil markers in the injected close data.

The economic calendar included a Chicago Fed National Activity Index reading for August at −0.04, below the 0.20 estimate and down from 0.08 prior.
Bill auctions also printed (3-month 4.0%, 6-month 4.2%).
The 10-year Treasury yield in the treasury snapshot dated 2026-09-18 was 5.0%, with a 2s10s spread of 0.25 percentage points.

Cross-asset moves were subdued relative to equities.
Gold futures ($GCUSD) −0.1% to 4,378.40.
The dollar proxy $UUP +0.3% to 28.48.
Bitcoin −1.2% to 85,521.99.
The VIX settled at 14.80, essentially flat (−0.1%) with an intraday band of 14.60–15.13.

Overseas indexes in the package were mixed to higher around the U.S. close context: Nikkei 225 +1.4%, FTSE 100 +0.7%, Hang Seng +0.4%, and the Germany ETF proxy $EWG +1.1% to 42.60.

The earnings calendar in the injection carried no reported results for this session.
News flow centered on UN-week diplomacy, U.S.–China meeting expectations, and oil headlines tied to Iran talk prospects — without replacing the hard close figures above.

Liquid gainers outside the mega-cap core included critical-minerals and thematic ETFs with large percentage moves; liquid losers included heavily short-beta products such as $DAMD (−19.7%) on the same day $AMD rallied nearly 10%.
